messages:
sarah: Heads-up — I ran the GPU ceil recalibration patch on staging for A100/H100 and we got an unexpected 8-12% p95 latency regression for medium-length requests when max_tokens_per_batch >= 4096.

jordan: Can you paste the exact numbers + which models and kernel choices? Also which queue policy was active?

sarah: Quick numbers: baseline p95=78ms, after=85-88ms (H100), throughput +4% for seq>2k. Affected models: red-nmt-1 / red-code-2. Kernel selector moved some slices from flash_attn -> gemm_fallback at seq_len ~1024. Queue policy: continuous batching with token_budget_target=0.7, max_tokens_per_batch=6144 (staging policy).

perf-bot: [auto-profile] run=2026-03-12T14:02Z gpu=h100 job=ceil-recal-2026-03-12

sarah: Inline profile excerpt:
```text
Model red-code-2 | seq=1024 | kernel=gemm_fallback | avg_token_ms=0.96 | p95_token_ms=1.12
Model red-code-2 | seq=1024 | kernel=flash_attn    | avg_token_ms=0.85 | p95_token_ms=0.92
KV-cache fragmentation: ~14% extra memcpy overhead for 2-slice packing
```

dina: Hmm, that smells like kernel selector thresholds + KV packing interaction. If flash_attn has better latency at that shape, why did selector choose fallback? Any metric for kernel fit score?

sarah: Selector had a tie-breaker toward better throughput for long sequences; it computed estimated_bytes_per_kv=1.1x which pushed some batches into fallback path. Also we saw larger KV-fragmentation when batch shapes mixed short+long.

nate: Quick thought — our continuous batcher pads/merges in a way that can increase effective seq_len for kernel decision. If padding pushes the median shape above flash_attn's sweet spot, selector will pick gemm. We should either tighten max_tokens_per_batch or bias selector to prefer lower-latency kernel for p95 SLOs.

marco: Agreed. Can we try two experiments: (A) lower H100 max_tokens_per_batch from 6144 -> 5632 and (B) change kernel_threshold for flash_attn from 1024 -> 768 (i.e., prefer flash_attn up to 768, fallback only above)?

jordan: +1 to both. Also add a KV alignment tweak: prefer packing with 128-token granularity to reduce fragmentation. Put each as independent flags so we can A/B.

perf-bot: experiment created: ceil-recal-h100-5632 (owner=dina) | ceil-recal-kernelthresh-768 (owner=nate)

dina: I'll run (A) today on staging and capture p50/p95/p99 + tail_gpu_util. Will also dump kernel-choice histogram.

sarah: For reference, here's the staging policy snippet I used: 
```json
{
  "continuous_batching": true,
  "token_budget_target": 0.7,
  "max_tokens_per_batch": 6144,
  "kernel_selector": {"prefer_throughput_for_long": true, "flash_attn_threshold": 1024}
}
```

jordan: If (A) reduces p95 to baseline and throughput drop is <2%, that's fine. If not, try (C) bias selector: add weight to latency in tie-breaker.

nate: Also, monitor KV cache hit ratio — if packing changes reduce cache reuse, we might regress further. Add kv_cache_hit_pct to dashboards for the run.

marco: Heads-up — A10/T4/L4 profiles look different. A10 seems happy with higher ceilings (4096+), T4/L4 need aggressive capping (2k-3k). We should run the same calibration across all card types but different target ceilings.

dina: Logging the experiment plan:
- H100: max_tokens_per_batch=5632, flash_attn_thresh=1024
- A100: run baseline vs 8192 ceil (compare)
- L4/T4: try 2048/3072 ceilings to reduce pad overhead

sarah: One more note: the kernel selector code path that estimates KV fragmentation is using a very coarse heuristic. We should instrument a per-batch kv_fragmentation_ratio metric (actual memcpy bytes / ideal bytes) to feed into selector next iteration.

jordan: Good. Let's keep the changescope minimal this week: only policy flags + better metrics. If experiments look good, follow up with selector logic change.

dina: Starting H100 job now. ETA for first results ~2 hours. Assigning follow-ups: @nate add kv_fragmentation metric; @marco coordinate L4/T4 runs.

sarah: Thanks. I'll watch staging dashboards and ping in this thread with numbers. :eyes:

perf-bot: [note] baseline_compare dashboard link: https://perf.internal/redwood/ceil-recal-compare (staging)

sarah: quick update (after 45m): H100 (5632) p95 back to 79ms, throughput -1.3% for long sequences, kernel-histogram shows flash_attn picks up ~35% of previously-fallbacked slices. KV_frag reduced from 14% -> 6%.

jordan: That's promising. Keep the run going and roll similar policy to A100 after we validate. Good call limiting the ceiling first. :thumbsup:
